name: Intro_Hello
description: Welcome slide to engage student and confirm readiness

ai_focus.eliciting_questions: Hi there! I'm Pi, and I'm super excited to explore fractions with you today! Are you ready to discover some really cool patterns?
ai_focus.goal: Establish rapport and confirm student engagement
ai_focus.initial_prompt_strategy: Warm greeting with enthusiasm for the topic

advance_to_next_slide_criteria: Student expresses readiness to start (says yes, ready, let's go, or similar positive response)

name: RealWorld_CandyBar_Observe
description: Image of a hand breaking a candy bar into two equal pieces

ai_focus.eliciting_questions: Let's start with this picture. What do you notice happening here?
ai_focus.potential_misconceptions: Focusing only on candy/hand, not the breaking action or equal pieces

guidance_prompts.condition: Student mentions candy but not breaking
guidance_prompts.prompt_text: Yes, I see the candy too! Tell me about what's happening to the candy bar.

guidance_prompts.condition: Student mentions breaking but not equal pieces
guidance_prompts.prompt_text: Great observation about the breaking! What do you notice about the size of those two pieces?

ai_focus.goal: Student identifies that candy bar is being broken into two equal pieces

advance_to_next_slide_criteria: Student identifies the candy bar has been broken into two equal pieces

name: RealWorld_Building_Count
description: Image of a building with 6 sections/floors, where 1 section is blue

ai_focus.eliciting_questions: Now let's look at this building. What details stand out to you?
potential_misconceptions: Counting windows instead of floor sections

guidance_prompts.condition: Student mentions building but doesn't count
guidance_prompts.prompt_text: Yes, it's a tall building! How would you describe the different sections or levels?

guidance_prompts.condition: Student counts but misses blue section
guidance_prompts.prompt_text: Nice counting! Now tell me about the colors you see.
Let's count together carefully. Can you point to each section as we count?

ai_focus.goal: Student counts 6 total sections and identifies 1 blue section
ai_focus.expected_student_response_pattern: States total of 6 sections/floors AND mentions 1 blue section

advance_to_next_slide_criteria: Student identifies the building has 6 total sections/floors and notes that one section is blue

name: Building_Fraction_Notation
prerequisites: Understanding of 6 total sections, 1 blue section
description: Same building image with fraction notation 1/6 showing the relationship

ai_focus.eliciting_questions: So we have 1 blue section out of 6 total sections. Mathematicians have a special way to write this relationship. What do you think 1/6 means?

guidance_prompts.prompt_text: The bottom number (6) tells us how many total sections there are. The top number (1) tells us how many are blue. Does that make sense?
Let's think about this step by step. How many sections are blue? How many sections in total?

ai_focus.goal: Student connects visual to fraction notation and understands 1 = blue part, 6 = total parts
ai_focus.expected_student_response_pattern: Shows understanding that 1 represents the blue section and 6 represents total sections

advance_to_next_slide_criteria: Student demonstrates understanding that 1 represents the blue section and 6 represents the total sections (connecting visual to notation)

name: Cake_Equal_Parts_Explore
description: Image of a round cake with one slice missing, showing equal divisions

ai_focus.eliciting_questions: Here's a cake that someone started sharing. What do you notice about how it was cut?
potential_misconceptions: Focusing only on missing slice, not equal divisions
Counting wrong number of total parts

guidance_prompts.condition: Student mentions missing slice but not equal parts
guidance_prompts.prompt_text: Yes, there's a missing slice! What do you notice about the size of all the slices?
Look carefully at each slice. Are they all the same size, or are some bigger than others?

ai_focus.goal: Student recognizes cake was cut into equal parts for fair sharing
ai_focus.expected_student_response_pattern: Identifies that cake is cut into equal-sized slices/parts

advance_to_next_slide_criteria: Student recognizes that the cake was cut into equal parts or equal-sized slices

name: Pattern_Summary_Celebration
description: Montage image showing candy bar, building, and cake with their fraction representations

ai_focus.eliciting_questions: Wow, look at all these examples together! What pattern do you see in the candy bar, building, and cake?
potential_misconceptions: Focusing on differences rather than similarities

guidance_prompts.prompt_text: In each picture, we're looking at parts of something whole. The candy bar has parts, the building has parts, and the cake has parts. What's the same about how we think about all of them?

ai_focus.goal: Student recognizes the common pattern of parts and wholes across all examples
ai_focus.expected_student_response_pattern: Identifies that all examples show parts of a whole or equal parts

advance_to_next_slide_criteria: Student identifies the common pattern that all examples show parts of a whole or demonstrates understanding of the fraction concept across different contexts
